featured_reviews.name: Shreyash Bidave
featured_reviews.review_text:
There are temples that you visit, and then there are temples that stay with you long after you leave. Shree Siddhivinayak Temple is one of those rare places.
The moment you step inside, the noise of Mumbai seems to fade away. Despite being one of the most visited temples in the country, there is a unique sense of peace and positivity that is difficult to describe in words. Standing before Lord Ganesha's idol, even for a few moments, brings a feeling of calmness, gratitude, and faith.
What makes Siddhivinayak special is not just its spiritual importance but the emotions attached to it. People from all walks of life come here with hopes, prayers, dreams, and gratitude. Whether you are a devotee or a first-time visitor, the divine atmosphere leaves a lasting impression.
The temple is well-maintained, organized, and managed efficiently despite the huge crowds. The discipline, cleanliness, and devotion of the devotees create an experience that feels both sacred and memorable.
For me, this wasn't just a temple visit—it was a reminder that faith has the power to bring peace even in the busiest city in India. The energy of this place is something that photographs cannot capture and words cannot fully explain. It is an experience that must be felt.
If you are visiting Mumbai, make time for Siddhivinayak. Whether your prayers are fulfilled today, tomorrow, or years later, you will leave with something valuable—a sense of peace in your heart.
"Mumbai has many landmarks, but Siddhivinayak is not just a landmark; it is the heartbeat of faith for millions." 🙏✨

featured_reviews.name: Lavi Bholwani
featured_reviews.review_text:
Shree Siddhivinayak Temple – A Place of Divine Energy in Mumbai

Visiting Siddhivinayak Temple in Mumbai is truly a soulful and uplifting experience. The moment you step inside, you can feel an incredible wave of positivity and spiritual energy surrounding you. The peaceful atmosphere, the sound of chants, and the sight of Lord Ganesha’s idol fill your heart with devotion and calmness.

The temple is beautifully maintained and well-organized despite the large number of devotees who visit every day. Whether you come seeking blessings, peace of mind, or simply a spiritual connection, the temple gives you a sense of super positive energy that stays with you long after you leave.

Another great convenience is the nearby metro station — ICICI Lombard Siddhivinayak Metro Station — which makes traveling to the temple very easy and hassle-free. The connectivity is excellent, especially for those who want to avoid Mumbai traffic.

Overall, Siddhivinayak Temple is not just a religious place; it’s a center of faith, positivity, and powerful divine vibes. A must-visit place in Mumbai for anyone looking to experience spiritual strength and inner peace. 🙏✨

featured_reviews.name: The Chartered Traveller
featured_reviews.review_text:
We went by cab, as parking around the temple is a big issue. Would definitely recommend visiting by cab/kali peeli if possible.

There are basically 3 queues for darshan:
1.	VIP Darshan
•	Around Rs 1500 for 4 people or Rs 500 for one person
•	Darshan usually in 2-5 minutes on weekdays
•	But darshan happens from the side view, not directly from the front
2.	Rs 100 Ticket Queue
•	Takes around 45 minutes to 1 hour
3.	Free Queue
•	Surprisingly, it took us only 34-36 minutes on a weekday
•	And the darshan was actually very good

Funny part was that the Rs 100 queue had more crowd than the free line. Last time we had taken the Rs 100 ticket and it took around 1 hour 15 minutes. This time we thought of trying the normal queue and were genuinely surprised.

Many agents or people around the temple may tell you that the normal line will take 2–4 hours and try to push paid tickets, but honestly, don’t fall into that trap, especially on weekdays.

The temple itself is amazing and very powerful. It is believed that the temple was established in 1801, and devotees believe that Lord Ganesha here fulfills wishes and removes obstacles, which is why lakhs of people visit every year. Even many celebrities and businessmen regularly come here before important events or new beginnings.

The pandits inside are good and cooperative. There is also a Hanuman temple near the exit, which is peaceful and worth visiting too.

Overall, a must visit temple in Mumbai, full of faith and positive energy.

featured_reviews.review_text:
The noble industrial sage and devoted social servant, Shri Bhagojis Kiir, who envisioned creation from nothingness, played a significant role in the social and cultural transformation of not just Dadar, but the entire city of Mumbai. Guided by his spiritual inspiration, in the year 1939, he established the sacred Shri Datt Mandir on T.H. Kataria Road in Mahim with deep devotion. Within this holy temple stands a marble idol of Shri Guru Dattatreya with a form centered on Lord Shiva. Since Shri Bhagojis Kiir’s revered deity was Shri Bhagweshwar Mahadev, it is believed that he chose this particular divine form for the temple accordingly. Born from his spiritual grace, this temple continues to be a revered center of faith to this day.

Avadhut Chintan Shri Gurudev

featured_reviews.name: Vishwesh Ranadive
featured_reviews.review_text:
Location: 5/5
Peaceful especially in the afternoon.
My Favourite place.

Mangal Murti Shree Gajanan means a vigilant and prosperous deity. Many have perceived this experience. Thousands of devotees visit the temple for “Darshan” and are blessed by our Shree Udyan Ganesh.

Initially, Shree Ganesh at this temple was underneath a banyan tree. Soon, this beautiful and radiant murti occupied the hearts of many devotees, specially because of its location with the sea as it’s backdrop. On the Magh Shuddha Chaturthi, Shake 1891 (Dated 09.02.1970) this Shree Ganesh came to be known as “SHREE UDYAN GANESH” which is the most apt name for it.

This beautiful temple with a small sanctum-sanctorum was built under the same banyan tree. During the construction of the temple, many hurdles were encountered, but after all the hardships and difficulties the temple of “Vighna Harta” materialized successfully. Today, this beautiful and holy temple is located under the same banyan tree. The surroundings of the temple including the adjoining area have been beautified and well maintained.
The Seva Samiti gives donation to many charitable organizations and also sponsors blood donation camps, diabetic checkups, eye care camps and cancer detection. In the temple, regular “Abhishek” and other religious rites are performed. As the occation demands, “Kirtans”, “Bhajans”, “Pravachan” are organized. Each year, “Shree Udyan Ganesh Janmotsav” is celebrated on a grand scale. Out of social concern, the Seva Samiti has also constructed a “Police Chowki” adjacently. Facility of cold drinking water has been made available for the public.

With the blessings of Shree Udyan Ganesh, all the activities and programs undertaken were successfully managed.

The Arulmigu Shree Maha Ganesar Alayam is the oldest Ganesh temple in Dharavi built in 1913 by Adi-Dravidar Southindian community . Managed by " B.S.I.A.S SANGH" The Bombay South Indian Adi-Dravida Mahajana Sangh was set up by migrants from Tirunelveli in Tamil Nadu who fled the plague and caste-ism of that era and come to Mumbai dharavi around 150-200 years ago where they set up Leather processing & tanneries industries.

The temple an important landmark in Dharavi, originally consisted of small shrine under the peepul tree. The Ganesha idol was brought & installed in this spot 1913.The building around it was only constructed in 1939 and the rest which consist of a Navagraha used for wedding and other ceremonial occasion.

CENTURION : THE OLDEST GANESH TEMPLE IN DHARAVI IS CELEBRATED ITS 100 YEARS OF GANESH FESTIVAL ON 2012. proudly know as DHARAVI CHA RAJA & DHARAVI CHA MAHARAJA / NAVSALA PAVNARA GANPATI

featured_reviews.review_text:
Inspiration for the people especially Maharashtra and South India. Shri. Vitthal Rukhmani Mandir is situated at Dadar West is the centr for the Kirtan kar (Who tell the spiritual knowledge).

Akhil Bhartiya Kirtan Sikshan santha is also run under this temple.

featured_reviews.name: Jiten Bhardwaj
featured_reviews.review_text: Good temple. Small and dainty. Idols are very nice and photographs of all gurus adorn the hall like how you have in Shirdi temple. Standing inside the main dome is nice feeling

featured_reviews.name: Sarwajit Jadhav
featured_reviews.review_text: Perfect place to meditate as it is pin drop silence inside but they have some spiritual group discussion on a few days of week between 8 to 10 pm otherwise it's good place to sit back and relax your mind.

featured_reviews.name: Prakash G Talreja
featured_reviews.review_text: This temple is located in the lane of Swami Samarth Temple..the street name is Col. Vaidya Marg...this is opposite Matoshree towers and Om Swami Anand building. This temple is a must visit for the replicas of statues of Shri Vithal and Rakhumai which you find in pandharpur. They celebrate all the festivals such as Ekadashi, and the pandharpur yatra days.

featured_reviews.name: shashikant jadhav
featured_reviews.review_text:
Old spacious temple. One can touch idols of God very rare. Ganpati Bappa. vitthal Rukumai ani Shivling are main idols.

They have kirtan classes regularly as well as classes to learn how to perform Pooja of Ganpati Bappa.

featured_reviews.name: Sonali Parab
featured_reviews.review_text: Very nice. There are kirtans from 4:15 -5:45 pm and anyone who is interested in learning kirtan then on 1st floor there's an अखिल भारतीय किर्तन संस्था
